features.name: Lump-sum prepayments
features.why: Extra you can pay each year without a charge, as a share of the original amount
features.rule: 20% or more a year: more flexible. 15%: typical. 10% or less: more limited.

features.name: Payment increases
features.why: How much you can raise your regular payment
features.rule: Up to 100% (double): more flexible. 15% to 99%: typical. 10% or less: more limited.

features.name: Double-up payments
features.why: Paying an extra amount, up to one more regular payment, on a payment date
features.rule: Offered: more flexible. Not offered: more limited.

features.name: How the fixed-rate penalty is worked out
features.why: For a fixed rate, the charge is usually the greater of three months' interest or the interest rate differential (IRD). Working out the IRD from posted rates usually makes it larger.
features.rule: IRD based on the rate you actually pay: more flexible. IRD based on posted rates: more limited.

features.name: Early renewal
features.why: How early you can renew without a prepayment charge
features.rule: 120 days or more before the term ends with no charge: more flexible. Fewer than 120 days: typical. A charge applies before the term ends: more limited.

features.name: Portable when you move
features.why: Taking your rate and remaining term to a new home without a prepayment charge
features.rule: Offered: more flexible. Not offered: more limited. Conditions are shown with the value.

features.name: Assumable by a buyer
features.why: A buyer taking over your mortgage, which can help when rates have gone up
features.rule: Offered: more flexible. Not offered: more limited.

features.name: Variable payments when prime changes
features.why: Whether your payment stays the same, with more or less going to interest, or changes with prime
features.rule: No mark: which is better depends on what you prefer.

features.name: Locking in to a fixed rate
features.why: Switching a variable rate to a fixed rate during the term
features.rule: Any fixed term, no charge: more flexible. No charge, but only to certain terms: typical. A charge applies or not offered: more limited.

features.name: Rate hold
features.why: How long a rate is guaranteed while you shop or wait to close
features.rule: 120 days or more: more flexible. 90 to 119 days: typical. Under 90 days: more limited.

features.name: Skipping a payment
features.why: Missing a payment when money is tight; interest still builds on it
features.rule: Offered: more flexible. Offered only after you've made an extra payment: typical. Not offered: more limited.

RBC Royal Bank.product: Closed fixed-rate mortgage (variable-rate features from its closed variable-rate mortgage)

lump.note: Of the original principal, once a year

double.note: From $100 up to one regular monthly payment, on any payment date

penalty.note: IRD uses RBC's posted rate less your rate reduction

renew.note: Early renewal option within 120 days of maturity

port.note: When buying and selling at the same time; borrow more at a blended rate

varpay.note: Payment is fixed for the term

lockin.note: Switch to a fixed rate without penalties

skip.note: Up to one monthly payment at a time, if not in arrears; skipped interest is added to the balance

TD Canada Trust.product: Closed fixed-rate mortgage (variable-rate features from its closed variable-rate mortgage)

lump.note: Of the original principal, once a year

penalty.note: IRD uses the posted rate for a similar mortgage, minus any discount you received

renew.note: Earlier renewal may mean a charge

port.note: Principal, rate, remaining term and amortization move to the new home, with no prepayment charge

varpay.note: The interest portion goes up if TD prime rises

lockin.note: At least the lesser of 3 years or the rest of the term; TD doesn't say whether there's a charge

skip.note: The equivalent of one monthly payment, subject to approval; interest continues

Scotiabank.product: 3, 4, 5, 7 and 10-year closed-term fixed-rate mortgages (variable-rate features from its Ultimate Variable Rate closed-term mortgage)

increase.note: Of the payment set for the term, each year

double.note: Match-a-Payment: an extra regular payment on any payment date

penalty.note: IRD uses Scotiabank's current posted rate, less any discount you received

port.note: May keep the rate for the rest of the term; the new home must meet Scotiabank's standards

varpay.note: Set using a cap rate for the whole term

lockin.note: Early renewal to a closed fixed term of 3 years or longer, with no prepayment charge

skip.note: Miss-a-Payment, if you've made a Match-a-Payment earlier in the term

BMO.product: BMO Smart Fixed Mortgage, the rate this site shows (other BMO closed mortgages allow 20% prepayments)

penalty.note: IRD uses BMO's current rate for a similar mortgage, reduced by any discount you received

renew.note: BMO says a prepayment charge applies if you renew before the end of the term

port.note: Fixed-rate closed mortgages, to a new mortgage of the same type; borrow more at a blended rate

assume.note: With BMO's approval; you're released once the buyer qualifies

CIBC.product: Fixed-rate closed mortgage (variable-rate features from its Variable Flex Mortgage)

increase.note: Of your regular amount, at any time

penalty.note: IRD compares your rate plus any discount with CIBC's current posted rate

port.note: All CIBC mortgages except the Variable Flex Mortgage; borrow more at a blended rate

varpay.note: Unless the amortization would go past 40 years

lockin.note: To a closed fixed term of 3 years or longer, at any time, with no prepayment charge

National Bank.product: Closed fixed-rate mortgage (variable-rate features from its closed variable-rate mortgage)

lump.note: Of the original principal, each calendar year

double.note: Add up to one extra payment amount to a regular payment

penalty.note: IRD is the difference between the posted rate and the standard rate

lockin.note: No fees; National Bank sets a minimum length for the new fixed term
